gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 30 W adapter rule applies only to Apple's own MagSafe Charger: the third-party Qi2 25W chargers need a bigger brick for an iPhone 17 to get 25 W (ESR Cyclone ≥35 W input; UGREEN MagFlow Pro pad '45W Adapter Required'; Anker Prime A25N1 a 45 W+ single-port USB-C adapter). It also doesn't say that an older MagSafe Charger (A2140) or a Qi2 15W-tier pad holds an iPhone 17 to 15 W.
standout_why: I compared against the cited apple.com/iphone-17/specs page, the Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m/2 m) store pages (they render only a title and test footnote) and ChatGPT's answer. They state only 'MagSafe up to 25W with 30W adapter' and 'Qi2 up to 25W'. None gives an adapter minimum for third-party Qi2 25W chargers. None names the old 15 W MagSafe part number (A2140) or the 25 W ones (A3502/A3503/A2580/A3250). None says that iPhone 17e tops out at 15 W, or how to tell a Qi2 25W charger from a 15W one (WPC record v2.2.1 / MPP25). ChatGPT closes by asking whether an existing charger can deliver 25 W, but none of its sources can answer that.
decides: It changes the total cost and therefore the pick. A shopper who already owns Apple's 30 W adapter gets 25 W only from Apple's MagSafe Charger. The ESR Cyclone needs ≥35 W, and the UGREEN MagFlow Pro pad and Anker Prime A25N1 need 45 W+, so each needs a new brick. Belkin WIZ040 ships with a 45 W PSU, so it works out of the box. A shopper with an iPhone 17e should not pay for 25 W at all, because Apple caps it at 15 W on MagSafe and on Qi2.

findings.label: Wireless charging ceilings and adapter condition
findings.value: MagSafe up to 25 W and Qi2 up to 25 W. MagSafe 25 W requires a 30 W or higher power adapter (footnote 6). Up to 50% in 30 min with a 30 W+ adapter and the MagSafe Charger
findings.note: Cited by ChatGPT. The 30 W condition in footnote 6 is attached to MagSafe charging.

findings.label: iPhone 17 tier and adapter needed for 25 W
findings.value: 25 W peak for iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (also 18 Pro / 18 Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max) with a 30 W+ adapter that outputs 15 V/2.0 A or more
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Same document: iPhone Air peaks at 20 W, and iPhone 16 / 16 Pro peak at 22.5 W.

findings.label: Which MagSafe Charger part numbers give 25 W vs 15 W
findings.value: 25 W: A3502, A3503, A2580 or A3250 (printed on the charger or its cable). 15 W: A2140
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple lists the 15 W tier as needing a 20 W+ USB-C adapter (9 V/2.22 A or 9 V/2.56 A) and the A2140 charger. An owner can check the number on their own cable to see whether it can do 25 W.

findings.label: iPhone 17 cap with a USB-C accessory connected
findings.value: 16 W when a USB-C accessory (e.g. wired headphones) is connected to an iPhone 17 or iPhone Air; 10 W for 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple gives the reason as complying with 'regulatory standards'. Apple also says that with both MagSafe and a cable attached, the iPhone charges through the cable.

findings.label: Connection order for full power
findings.value: Plug the charger into power before placing the iPhone on it. If the iPhone went on first, remove it, wait 3 s and replace it to resume maximum power
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Stated by Apple. It is a common reason for 'my 25 W charger only does 15 W'.

findings.label: Wireless ceiling (exclusion from 25 W)
findings.value: MagSafe up to 15 W and Qi2 up to 15 W, with a 20 W adapter or higher
findings.note: Footnote 11 covers both MagSafe and Qi2. support.apple.com/en-us/105047 also puts iPhone 17e in the 15 W tier.

findings.value: Up to 25 W for iPhone 18/17, 16 Pro Max / 16 Plus with ≥35 W input; 20 W for iPhone Air / 16 Pro / 16 with ≥35 W; 15 W for iPhone 15–12 with ≥20 W. iOS 26 or later for iPhone 16+ (not 16e). Magnetic case ≤2 mm; not compatible with non-magnetic cases, grips/stands, metal accessories or wallets

findings.value: 45 W USB-C PSU and 1.5 m braided USB-C cable included. Qi2 iPhones (16 and later) charge at 25 W; MagSafe iPhones 12–15 at 15 W. Apple Watch fast charging on Series 7+ and Ultra; AirPods up to 5 W

findings.note: Price $129.99. Belkin's 0–50% in 25 min footnote was tested on iPhone 16 with iOS 26 or newer. The page gives no case-thickness limit.

findings.label: Adapter, iOS and case requirements
findings.value: 'Requires a 45W or higher adapter to achieve full 25W output'; FAQ: 'original or single-port USB-C adapter rated at 45W or higher'. Input 9 V⎓3 A / 12 V⎓3 A / 15 V⎓3 A. iPhone 16 series and later on iOS 26+ are Qi2.2 compatible. 16 Pro Max / 16 Plus 25 W, 16 / 16 Pro 22 W, Air 20 W, earlier iPhones up to 15 W. Not compatible with iPhone 16e. MagSafe-compatible case ≤2.5 mm. Not compatible with Samsung Galaxy Watch
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Wireless Charging Station (3-in-1, MagGo, AirCool, Foldable) - Anker US
findings.note: Price $149.99 ('Save $30.00'). The page does not say an adapter is in the box. Our current page's 'Yes, 45 W' cell for Anker is not supported by this page. The single-port wording means a shared multi-port GaN brick may not deliver 25 W.

findings.label: How to tell a Qi2 25W charger from a 15 W Qi2 one
findings.value: In the WPC Qi database, a 25 W product shows Version 2.2.1 and Power Profile MPP25. A record showing 2.0.0, MPP or 15.0 is 'Qi2 but it is the 15W tier'. 'The iPhone 17 line does [25 W] natively, and the iPhone 16 series does on iOS 26'
findings.source_title: Qi2 25W Charging Stations You Should Know About (Wireless Power Consortium)
findings.note: The WPC page says Qi2 15W stations are 'a different product'. The page carries no publication date beyond © 2026.
